items.note: New GLOBAL partial `styles/_surface-motion.scss` holds the shared entrance keyframes (ds-fade-in, ds-scale-in, ds-slide-in, ds-slide-edge-in) that every DS surface now names through --ds-<surface>-enter-keyframes. Consumers of the bundled entry (`@use 'styles/ds';`) need NO change — ds.scss forwards it. Only à-la-carte consumers that @use DS partials individually must add it, next to `styles/overlay-motion`: without it the keyframes do not exist and modal / drawer / bottom-sheet / toast / banner / alert / loading-overlay / overlay panels render with no entrance (silently — no error). Order does not matter; @use anywhere in the styles entry is enough. If a consumer's styles.scss has no `styles/overlay-motion` line, add `@use 'styles/surface-motion';` beside whatever DS partials it does @use.

`ds-table` no longer nulls `sortKey` when the sort cycle reaches "unsorted" — the key keeps naming the column the user last touched and `sortDir === null` alone means unsorted. Fixes a header desync for hosts that map "off" back to their own default sort. ACTION: any host that treats a non-null `sortKey` as "a sort is active" must gate on `sortDir` instead — e.g. `if (sortKey())` becomes `if (sortDir())`, and a server query built as `orderBy: sortKey()` must skip the clause when `sortDir()` is null. Hosts that already read both, or that pass `sortingOrder: ['asc','desc']` (no unsorted state), need no change. The table's own rendering (icons, aria-sort) and its client-side sorting were already gated on `sortDir` and are unchanged.

Every message-bearing field now defaults `reserveMessage` to FALSE (was true since 0.7.0). The resolution chain is unchanged - per-field input, then `DS_CONFIG.field.reserveMessage`, then the default - only the final fallback flipped. VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE: a field with no hint/error no longer holds a message line, so a form gets ~23px shorter per field and the controls below shift down the first time a hint or error appears. Affects all 14 fields: input, textarea, select, autocomplete, multi-select, checkbox, radio, radio-group, switch, slider, date-picker, time-picker, color-picker, otp-input. ACTION: a form that validates and must not reflow should turn it back on. App-wide in one line - `provideDsConfig({ field: { reserveMessage: true } })` - which is also how to restore 0.7.0 behaviour exactly; or per field with `[reserveMessage]="true"`. Consumers that had written `[reserveMessage]="false"` to opt OUT can delete those bindings, and any tighter sub-stack added to compensate for the reserved gap (e.g. a `var(--space-1)` wrapper) should be re-checked - with the row collapsed, a normal 16px stack is correct again.

A nested `provideDsConfig` (on a Route, component or directive) now MERGES with the config above it, section by section, instead of replacing it wholesale. Previously the provider used `useValue`, so a subtree that set one flag silently reset every unrelated section to its default. NO ACTION for the normal case - a single root-level `provideDsConfig` behaves exactly as before, and nested provision was neither documented nor safe to use. Only relevant if a consumer deliberately relied on a nested call to RESET a section back to defaults: that now needs the section spelled out explicitly, e.g. `provideDsConfig({ datePicker: { locale: 'en-US', dateFormat: undefined, firstDayOfWeek: 1 } })`. Enables the new `dsReserveMessages` directive to scope one field flag without disturbing the rest.

informational: Purely additive, opt-in inputs — no consumer action: `ds-table` [rowId] accessor (row identity for tracking/selection/expansion; still defaults to row.id), `ds-date-picker`/`ds-time-picker` [fullWidth], `ds-pagination` [showPageSize], and public `focus(options?)` on `ds-search` / `ds-input` / `ds-textarea`.

`ds-table`'s row generic relaxes from `{ id: string }` to `object` so keyless data can supply [rowId]; rows that keep an `id` type-check exactly as before, and the resolver is public as `rowKey(row)`.

New override tokens, all defaulting to the current values: --ds-<surface>-enter-keyframes / -enter-duration / -enter-easing (+ -enter-offset / -enter-scale) and -leave-duration / -leave-easing across overlay panels, modal, drawer, bottom sheet, toast, banner, alert and loading overlay; --ds-modal-eyebrow-* (5); --ds-modal-title-font-size; --ds-date-picker-trigger-radius; --ds-date-picker-panel-radius; --ds-checkbox-radius; --ds-popover-min-width; --ds-menu-min-width / -max-width; --ds-toast-min-width / -max-width; --ds-table-cell-pad-{top,right,bottom,left}; --ds-table-head-border-color / -weight / -tracking; --ds-pagination-label-font-size / -weight / -color.
`ds-modal` / `ds-modal-card` gained an `[eyebrow]` projection slot above the title; unfilled it renders nothing, so existing dialogs are unaffected.

`DS_CONFIG` gained a `field.reserveMessage` key — `provideDsConfig({ field: { reserveMessage: false } })` sets the message-row default for all 14 message-bearing fields. The per-field input still wins; its type widens to `boolean | null` (null = not set), so existing bindings and bare attributes behave identically.

Visual-only: overlay panels now enter FROM their trigger edge (a panel above its trigger rises instead of sliding down), a selected dropdown option keeps its tint under hover/keyboard-active, and a read-only `ds-modal` no longer draws an empty footer strip.
ds-time-picker gained label / required / optional inputs (additive) — a date + time form row now aligns without a hand-rolled label; existing usages without label render exactly as before.

Visual-only in ds-time-picker: the clock glyph moved from before the value to the trailing edge and grew 14px -> 16px, the value weight dropped from medium to regular, and the trigger gap narrowed 8px -> 4px, all to match ds-date-picker / ds-select / ds-input. Recover the old weight with --ds-time-picker-value-weight: var(--font-weight-medium).

Value typography of both pickers is now tokenised: --ds-date-picker-value-font-family / -font-size / -weight (mono default, shared with the ghost mask) and --ds-time-picker-value-font-family / -font-size / -weight, plus --ds-time-picker-required-color. Defaults unchanged except the time value weight noted above.
ds-date-picker [fullWidth] now pushes the calendar glyph to the trailing edge instead of leaving it packed beside the value; only affects fields that opt into fullWidth.
